entry.title: Creating Opportunities in the Maritime Transition for Latin America and the Caribbean
entry.summary:
LONDON, November 26 (IPS) - The COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Türkiye comes at a decisive moment for humanity. We are now grappling with a scenario in which the Paris Agreement goal of limiting global warming to 1.5 °C will not be met, which brings the concept of “overshoot” to the fore. The best current aspiration is to limit the extent of that overshoot, peak emissions as soon as possible, and then return to 1.5 °C.

entry.title: Will Bangladesh’s Islamists Reconcile with the Nation’s Cultural Identity?
entry.summary:
DHAKA, Bangladesh, November 25 (IPS) - Bangladesh has now been let down by two governments in a row. Sixteen years of Awami League rule ended in corruption and authoritarianism, and the BNP, returned to power, is behaving much as its predecessor did. The Islamist party presents itself as the clean alternative, yet many voters fear its views on women and its opposition to parts of Bengali culture. This essay argues that Bangladesh’s strength has always lain in its culture, ex cultu robur, and that the Islamist party’s future depends on whether it can make peace with that inheritance.

Read the full story, “Will Bangladesh’s Islamists Reconcile with the Nation’s Cultural Identity?”, on globalissues.org →
